A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sufficient-context RAG study. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed material to be compared reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original autorater evaluations, RAG performance analyses, context-length experiments, selective-generation results, and fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds human-label-based performance analysis and comparisons between lexical and LLM-based answer evaluation.

M1.justification: The sufficient-context autoraters, FLAMe chunking, confidence-plus-sufficiency logistic regression, abstention thresholds, and three fine-tuning mixtures remain unchanged. The completed one-shot prompt documents an existing component rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: The named datasets and QA tasks remain unchanged. However, new Table 4 evaluates an unnamed curated set of context-dependent questions without explicitly connecting it to the existing 115-example annotation set. Whether this adds distinct data coverage or reuses earlier data cannot be established.

E2.justification: Table 3 loses the Llama 3.1 8B comparisons, while new Table 4 includes Gemini 1.5 Flash alongside previously evaluated models. The autorater comparators in Table 1 and confidence-only selective-generation comparator remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation stratified by human sufficiency labels and a supplementary response-based Contains Answer metric. It also removes the Llama fine-tuning configuration. The retained experiments preserve their sample counts, context limits, retrieval settings, LoRA parameters, and training budgets; relocated preprocessing descriptions do not establish protocol changes.

E4.justification: New Table 4 examines model behavior using human sufficiency labels, and Appendix B.3 tests dependence on the answer evaluator across three datasets, including concrete lexical-matching failure cases. These substantially expand checks on the reliability of the central analysis. The Mistral fine-tuning ablations remain, while their Llama counterparts disappear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or seed-based uncertainty summaries. The repeated answer sampling used to calculate P(True) is unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results under human sufficiency labels and lexical answer scoring, and removes all Llama rows from Table 3. For example, new Table 4 reports Gemini 1.5 Pro correctness of 84.1% with sufficient context and 9.6% with insufficient context; these are additional results, not same-setting performance changes. Retained main figures, Table 1, and Mistral scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The sufficient-context definition, its relationship to entailment, and the conditions in Remarks 1–3 remain unchanged. Ambiguity examples are moved and renamed, and factuality considerations receive additional explanation. Neither version adds mathematical proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the proprietary-versus-open-source distinction with a distinction based on model size and baseline performance. Fine-tuning claims are narrowed to Mistral after removing Llama. The central contributions, 93% autorater accuracy, and claimed 2–10% selective-generation benefit remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains why sufficiency can permit factually incorrect context, connecting this choice to inference without ground truth and label noise. Appendix B.3 adds interpretations of lexical-matching failures and metric robustness. Future-work discussion is revised to include context ranking and multimodal QA, while the existing QA-focused limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 replaces placeholder demonstration content with a concrete one-shot question, references, explanation, and label, and completes the query/context template. The abstract and introduction also add a GitHub access pointer for findings and prompts. These improve documentation without establishing changed experimental procedures or independently verifying external availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Paes et al. (2022) and Joren et al. (2023) on disaggregated performance, and Joren et al. (2024) alongside abstention thresholding. It removes the Llama technical-report reference with the Llama experiments. The broader positioning against relevance, entailment, and hallucination research remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Detailed fine-tuning material moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix B.1, evaluation explanations move into the prompt appendices, and future work moves into the conclusion with revisions. Local explanations, acknowledgments, author footnotes, and conference headers are added.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4 and 5, shortens and relocates Table 3, places Figures 5 and 6 together, and expands the prompt-box layouts. The existing figures and Tables 1–2 retain their designs, with limited caption and placement changes rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.3 provides useful evidence about dependence on answer grading, and the concrete one-shot example improves reproducibility of the central autorater. These strengthen the paper beyond v1. Removing Llama fine-tuning results reduces empirical breadth, and Table 4's unclear dataset provenance limits its value, so the overall improvement is limited.
